log.text: Light Screen up on P1's side
Light Screen ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Mega Gengar leads with Klefki for priority Reflect. Gengar-Mega outspeeds the field T1 and Shadow Tag traps both foes — use Shadow Ball (100% acc, not Focus Blast which cost Game 1). Klefki follows with Prankster TWave on Scarf Rotom-W or Light Screen. Once key threat is removed, Gyarados enters behind screens to DD sweep. Rotom-Heat back gives EQ immunity and WoW for physical attackers. Gengar Ghost typing blanks Blaziken Close Combat.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Klefki+Gengar-Mega lead, Gyarados+Rotom-Heat back. Shadow Tag traps threats esp Scarf Rotom-W (4x Volt Switch on Gyarados). Use Shadow Ball not Focus Blast (70% acc cost Game 1). Gyarados +1 Spe (219) does NOT outspeed max Scarf Rotom-W (226.5) — need TWave or +2 Spe. Klefki Prankster TWave outprioritizes Rotom-W Volt Switch. Gengar-Mega Ghost immune to Blaziken Close Combat. Rotom-Heat Levitate immune to EQ, WoW burns Garchomp/Blaziken. Opp may bring Rotom-W/Blaziken (unseen Game 1). Opp Protect frequency high — double-attack to punish stalls. Archaludon Steel blocks Shadow Ball — need Focus Blast or Gyarados Waterfall for it.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Gengar-Mega. Lead with Tinkaton and Archaludon because both resist Gengar's STABs and Fairy moves, safely handling Gengar-Mega turn 1. They also cover Aegislash and Klefki with super-effective attacks, and threaten Gyarados with Thunderbolt and Play Rough. Blaziken and Rotom-Wash provide Speed Boost sweeping and Choice Scarf speed control for the mid-to-late game once Shadow Tag is removed.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega is opponent's intended Mega (Shadow Tag). Tinkaton and Archaludon resist Gengar's STABs and Fairy moves, safest lead. Aegislash is Brave, likely uses King's Shield to drop Attack. Ditto has Imposter Choice Scarf, transforms into Garchomp if switched in. Rotom-Heat is Levitate Expert Belt Timid, immune to EQ, weak to Rock Slide. Garchomp must survive to KO Aegislash last. Plan: Use Tinkaton/Archaludon to break Gengar/Aegislash/Klefki, then clean up with Blaziken or Rotom-Wash. Keep Garchomp healthy for endgame.

selection: Light Screen (your side, including ally Gengar)
decisions.rationale: Light Screen (Prankster) goes up first, cutting Dark Pulse to ~40-58% and preventing the OHKO on Gengar-Mega. Focus Blast is the only move that damages Archaludon (2x SE, 87-168%); Sturdy saves it at 1 HP, then Life Orb recoil KOs it after it attacks. Mega Evolving activates Shadow Tag, trapping both foes. Even if Focus Blast misses (30%), Light Screen + Shadow Tag keeps us in control. Shadow Ball/Sludge Bomb are NVE/immune on both targets.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Klefki+Gengar-Mega lead, Gyarados+Rotom-Heat back. Shadow Tag traps threats esp Scarf Rotom-W (4x Volt Switch on Gyarados). Use Shadow Ball not Focus Blast (70% acc cost Game 1). Gyarados +1 Spe (219) does NOT outspeed max Scarf Rotom-W (226.5) — need TWave or +2 Spe. Klefki Prankster TWave outprioritizes Rotom-W Volt Switch. Gengar-Mega Ghost immune to Blaziken Close Combat. Rotom-Heat Levitate immune to EQ, WoW burns Garchomp/Blaziken. Opp may bring Rotom-W/Blaziken (unseen Game 1). Opp Protect frequency high — double-attack to punish stalls. Archaludon Steel blocks Shadow Ball — need Focus Blast or Gyarados Waterfall for it. Gengar-Mega stats: HP136 Atk76 Def100 SpA222 SpD115 Spe200. Archaludon Dark Pulse can OHKO Gengar-Mega (80-116%) without Light Screen — always screen first vs special SE threats. Tinkaton Knock Off does 36-56% to Gengar-Mega. Focus Blast on Archaludon does 88-168% but Sturdy saves it at 1HP; Life Orb recoil finishes it. Mold Breaker does NOT bypass Shadow Tag trapping.

decisions.rationale: Gyarados provides Intimidate to cut Tinkaton's physical output, keeping Klefki safe. Ground immunity vs Garchomp EQ and Protect to scout Rotom-W are key. If Scarf Rotom-W comes in, Klefki Prankster TWave outprioritizes Volt Switch. Gyarados is also the primary DD win condition for lategame. Rotom-Heat is weaker to Rock Slide spread and lacks Intimidate's defensive value.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, but Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat remain vs Tinkaton+4 unseen (Garchomp/Arcanine/Rotom-W/Blaziken). Waterfall only neutral on Garchomp (Dragon resists). Rotom-Heat Overheat is 2x SE on Tinkaton. Garchomp Rock Slide is 2x SE on Rotom-Heat. Klefki Prankster TWave outprioritizes Scarf Rotom-W Volt Switch — key speed control tool. Light Screen up 8 turns. Plan: TWave Tinkaton next turn with Klefki, DD with Gyarados if safe. Preserve Rotom-Heat for Garchomp/Blaziken matchups (Levitate EQ immune, WoW burns physicals). Opp Protect frequency high — double attack to punish.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon Dark Pulse (67-158%) + Tinkaton Knock Off (24-58%) likely KO Gengar-Mega turn 1, removing Shadow Tag. Both resist Gengar STABs. Klefki Prankster T-Wave may paralyze Archaludon but 75% it still moves. Aggressive play breaks their core fastest.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega intended Mega (Shadow Tag). Tinkaton/Archaludon resist Gengar STABs, safest lead vs Gengar/Klefki. Aegislash Brave, likely King's Shield to drop Attack. Ditto Imposter Choice Scarf, transforms into switched-in Pokémon. Rotom-Heat Levitate Expert Belt Timid, weak to Rock Slide. Plan: break Gengar/Aegislash/Klefki with Tinkaton/Archaludon, clean with Blaziken/Rotom-Wash. Keep Garchomp healthy for endgame vs Aegislash.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is immune to Klefki's Prankster Thunder Wave, outspeeds with Choice Scarf, and threatens Gyarados. Tinkaton Protects to preserve HP and scout. Blaziken risks paralysis and can't hit Klefki hard.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega intended Mega (Shadow Tag). Tinkaton/Archaludon resist Gengar STABs. Aegislash Brave, likely King's Shield. Ditto Imposter Choice Scarf transforms into switched-in Pokémon. Rotom-Heat Levitate Expert Belt Timid, weak to Rock Slide. Plan: break Gengar/Aegislash/Klefki with Tinkaton/Archaludon, clean with Blaziken/Rotom-Wash. Keep Garchomp healthy for endgame vs Aegislash. Game 2: Archaludon fainted turn 1. Klefki Prankster, Light Clay, Light Screen up. Rotom-Wash Choice Scarf immune to T-Wave, outspeeds Klefki. Blaziken Focus Sash Speed Boost Jolly. Tinkaton Mold Breaker Sitrus Berry Careful.

decisions.rationale: Scarf Rotom-W Volt Switch OHKOs Gyarados (101-147%). Gyarados must Protect. Klefki Prankster TWave (+1 priority) outspeeds everything and paralyzes Tinkaton, giving permanent speed control. Can't TWave Rotom-W (Electric immunity). Klefki is safe: Tinkaton's Knock Off/Play Rough are 0.25x/0.5x on Steel/Fairy at -1 Atk. Next turn: if Rotom-W locked into Volt Switch, switch Gyarados to Rotom-Heat (resists Electric); if Tinkaton paralyzed, Gyarados can DD safely.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat vs Tinkaton+Rotom-W(Scarf)+Garchomp(EBelt)+Arcanine(Leftovers)+Blaziken(Sash). Rotom-W is Electric = immune to TWave. Volt Switch 4x OHKOs Gyarados — must Protect or switch to Rotom-Heat (resists Electric). Klefki is extremely safe vs Tinkaton (all attacks NVE on Steel/Fairy). Plan: TWave Tinkaton for speed control, then DD Gyarados if safe or pivot to Rotom-Heat for Garchomp/Blaziken matchups. Rotom-Heat Overheat 2x SE on Tinkaton. Preserve Rotom-Heat as Garchomp answer (Levitate EQ immune, Overheat 2x on Steel). Opp Protect frequency high — punish with double attacks when safe.

decisions.rationale: Volt Switch is 4x SE with STAB into Gyarados, guaranteed massive damage or KO. Tinkaton Protects from Klefki's Prankster priority, staying safe. After Volt Switch, we bring in Blaziken with Focus Sash to clean up Klefki and handle remaining threats. This maintains momentum and removes the immediate Dragon Dance threat.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega intended Mega (Shadow Tag). Aegislash Brave, likely King's Shield. Ditto Imposter Choice Scarf transforms into switched-in Pokémon. Rotom-Heat Levitate Expert Belt Timid, weak to Rock Slide. Plan: break Gengar/Aegislash/Klefki with Tinkaton/Archaludon, clean with Blaziken/Rotom-Wash. Keep Garchomp healthy for endgame vs Aeglislab. Game 2: Archaludon fainted turn 1. Klefki Prankster, Light Clay, Light Screen up. Rotom-Wash Choice Scarf immune to T-Wave, outspeeds Klefki. Blaziken Focus Sash Speed Boost Jolly. Tinkaton Mold Breaker Sitrus Berry Careful. Opponent leads Klefki + Gyarados; Klefki sets screens, Gyarados physical attacker Life Orb Jolly.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-W is Choice-locked into Volt Switch (4x on Gyarados). Switching to Rotom-Heat resists Electric (10-26% chip) and preserves Gyarados for later. Klefki Prankster TWave on Tinkaton is +1 priority; Tinkaton Protect is reduced to ~33% so TWave likely lands, permanently crippling Tinkaton's speed. Even if blocked, Rotom-Heat is in safely and we retry next turn at lower Protect odds. Worst case both foes hit Rotom-Heat for ~50% total — survivable with screens up.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat vs Tinkaton+Rotom-W(Scarf)+Garchomp(EBelt)+Arcanine(Leftovers)+Blaziken(Sash). Rotom-W is Electric = immune to TWave. Volt Switch 4x OHKOs Gyarados — must Protect or switch to Rotom-Heat (resists Electric). Klefki is extremely safe vs Tinkaton (all attacks NVE on Steel/Fairy). Plan: TWave Tinkaton for speed control, then DD Gyarados if safe or pivot to Rotom-Heat for Garchomp/Blaziken matchups. Rotom-Heat Overheat 2x SE on Tinkaton. Preserve Rotom-Heat as Garchomp answer (Levitate EQ immune, Overheat 2x on Steel). Opp Protect frequency high — punish with double attacks when safe. Rotom-Heat resists Volt Switch (10-26% from Scarf Rotom-W). Tinkaton atk -1 from Intimidate. Garchomp is Ground = immune to TWave. Blaziken has Focus Sash + Speed Boost — must break sash before it sweeps.

decisions.rationale: Rotom is locked into Volt Switch. Double targeting Gyarados with Tinkaton's Play Rough and Rotom's 4x SE Volt Switch maximizes the chance to KO the Life Orb threat before it can Dragon Dance or attack.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega intended Mega. Aegislash Brave King's Shield. Ditto Imposter Choice Scarf. Rotom-Heat Expert Belt Timid. Game 2: Archaludon fainted turn 1. Klefki Prankster Light Clay, Light Screen up. Rotom-Wash Choice Scarf locked into Volt Switch. Blaziken Focus Sash Speed Boost Jolly. Tinkaton Mold Breaker Sitrus Berry Careful. Gyarados Life Orb Jolly.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Overheat chunks/KOs Tinkaton (71-125%, possible OHKO). Prankster Reflect deploys before Blaziken attacks, cutting Flare Blitz to ~37-80% so Klefki survives double-targets. If Blaziken Protects for Speed Boost, it can't Protect next turn — Klefki Prankster TWave lands then. Overheat SpA drop is acceptable since Rotom-Heat can pivot to WoW/Tbolt or switch out to reset.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat vs Tinkaton+Blaziken+Rotom-W(Scarf). Rotom-W Scarf Volt Switch 4x OHKOs Gyarados — must Protect or switch to Rotom-Heat. Klefki extremely safe vs Tinkaton (all attacks NVE on Steel/Fairy). Tinkaton has Mold Breaker — TWave hits through Levitate on Rotom-Heat. Blaziken Focus Sash + Speed Boost — must break sash or burn/para before it sweeps. Blaziken can't Protect twice in a row — Klefki Prankster TWave guaranteed next turn if it Protects now. Overheat 2x SE on Tinkaton (Fire vs Steel 2x, vs Fairy 1x = 2x net). Flare Blitz 2x SE on Klefki (Fire vs Steel 2x, vs Fairy 1x = 2x net). Plan: KO Tinkaton, Reflect up, TWave Blaziken next turn, preserve Rotom-Heat for Garchomp/Rotom-W matchups, DD Gyarados if safe opening arises.

decisions.rationale: Flare Blitz is 2x effective on Klefki (Steel/Fairy), and Tinkaton Protect shields it from Rotom-Heat's Overheat. Blaziken outspeeds Klefki (145 vs 95-127) and likely Rotom-Heat (116-151 range). This maintains offensive pressure while minimizing risk, keeping both Pokémon healthy to handle Gyarados switch-in next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Archaludon fainted turn 1 to Gengar Focus Blast. Gengar-Mega KO'd turn 1 by Archaludon Dark Pulse + Tinkaton Knock Off. Klefki Prankster Light Clay, Light Screen up (5 turns). Rotom-Heat Expert Belt Timid 77% after Tinkaton Play Rough turn 3. Blaziken Focus Sash Speed Boost Jolly just entered turn 3. Tinkaton Mold Breaker Sitrus Berry Careful paralyzed turn 3, Atk -1 from Gyarados Intimidate turn 1. Opponent back: Gyarados Life Orb Jolly. Rotom-Wash Choice Scarf Timid available. Plan: KO Klefki with Blaziken Fighting/Fire moves, then handle Gyarados with Rotom-Wash or Blaziken depending on boosts. Gyarados threatens Waterfall/Crunch/Dragon Dance. Aegislash Brave and Ditto Imposter not brought Game 2.

decisions.rationale: Klefki Prankster TWave (priority +1) outpaces Blaziken's attack, crippling its sweep even if Klefki dies to Flare Blitz after. Overheat 2x SE on Tinkaton (71-154% range) likely KOs or heavily damages. Reflect halves Blaziken's Close Combat on Rotom to ~25-44%, so Rotom survives at 78%. If Blaziken Protects, it can't next turn and Klefki retries TWave. Gyarados preserved as wincon.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat vs Tinkaton+Blaziken+Rotom-W(Scarf). Rotom-W Scarf Volt Switch 4x OHKOs Gyarados — must Protect or switch to Rotom-Heat. Klefki extremely safe vs Tinkaton (all attacks NVE on Steel/Fairy). Tinkaton has Mold Breaker — TWave hits through Levitate on Rotom-Heat. Blaziken Focus Sash broken (at 74% from Flare Blitz recoil, sash no longer active). Blaziken Speed Boost — must para/burn before it outspeeds everything. Prankster TWave on Klefki outpaces Blaziken at +1 speed. Reflect halves physical damage (7 turns), Light Screen (4 turns). Plan: KO Tinkaton with Overheat, TWave Blaziken, preserve Rotom-Heat for Rotom-W matchup, DD Gyarados if safe opening arises.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Blaziken Flare Blitz KO's Klefki at 23% even through Reflect (super-effective STAB). Tinkaton Protects to avoid Rotom-Heat Overheat; even with reduced success rate, it's safer than taking 130-power super-effective hit. Removes Klefki's Prankster paralysis threat and sets up Blaziken to clean Rotom-Heat next turn with Close Combat or Rotom-Wash switch.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Archaludon fainted turn 1 to Gengar Focus Blast. Gengar-Mega KO'd turn 1 by Archaludon Dark Pulse + Tinkaton Knock Off. Klefki Prankster Light Clay, Light Screen + Reflect up. Rotom-Heat Expert Belt Timid 77% after Tinkaton Play Rough turn 3. Blaziken Speed Boost Jolly Focus Sash, Speed +1. Tinkaton Mold Breaker Sitrus Berry Careful paralyzed turn 3, Atk -1 from Gyarados Intimidate turn 1. Opponent back: Gyarados Life Orb Jolly. Rotom-Wash Choice Scarf Timid available. Plan: KO Klefki with Blaziken Flare Blitz, then handle Rotom-Heat with Blaziken Close Combat or Rotom-Wash. Gyarados threatens Waterfall/Crunch/Dragon Dance. Aegislash Brave and Ditto Imposter not brought Game 2.

decisions.rationale: Overheat guaranteed KOs Tinkaton (71-125% vs 38% HP) even at -2 SpA. Switching Klefki to Gyarados saves it from Flare Blitz KO, triggers Intimidate on both foes, and Gyarados resists both Blaziken STABs (0.5x). Even worst-case Blaziken Close Combat on Rotom-Heat does ~16-29% after Intimidate+Reflect. Rotom-Heat preserved as Rotom-W Volt Switch sponge.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat vs Tinkaton+Blaziken+Rotom-W(Scarf). Rotom-W Scarf Volt Switch 4x OHKOs Gyarados — must Protect or switch to Rotom-Heat. Rotom-Heat resists Volt Switch (0.5x Electric vs Electric typing) — best Rotom-W answer. Blaziken Focus Sash broken (74% from recoil). Blaziken Speed Boost accumulating — at +3 next turn (137-181 effective) may outspeed Rotom-Heat(138). Gyarados at 146 + DD needed to outspeed Scarf Rotom-W (174-226). Klefki at 23% — limited utility remaining (screens up, both foes para'd). Plan: KO Tinkaton T6, then DD Gyarados vs Blaziken (resists both STABs), Will-O-Wisp Blaziken if free turn, preserve Rotom-Heat for Rotom-W. Reflect 6t, Light Screen 3t remaining.

decisions.rationale: Blaziken's 145 Speed outsplits Klefki's 95-127, ensuring Flare Blitz KOs through Reflect. Switching to Rotom-Wash brings a full-HP Choice Scarf attacker that resists Rotom-Heat's Fire/Electric moves and outspeeds Gyarados to Hydro Pump it super effectively next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent leads Klefki (Prankster, Light Clay, used Reflect, Light Screen, Thunder Wave x3) and Rotom-Heat (Expert Belt, Timid, Overheat x2, SpA -2). Back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, Intimidate). Aegislash and Ditto not brought. My back: Rotom-Wash (Choice Scarf, Timid). Plan: Use Rotom-Wash to handle Rotom-Heat and Gyarados with Hydro Pump. Blaziken can Close Combat Rotom-Heat or Flare Blitz Gyarados if needed. Tinkaton is less useful due to paralysis and Atk -1.

decisions.rationale: Volt Switch guaranteed-OHKOs Gyarados so Protect is mandatory. Rotom-Heat at SpA-4 can't damage meaningfully; Will-O-Wisp on Blaziken is the highest-EV play — burn+Intimidate drops Blaziken to 0.25x Atk permanently. Opponent's natural line is Volt Switch into Gyarados (blocked), then WoW lands. Risk: opponent predicts Protect and Hydro Pumps Rotom-Heat (80% acc, possible OHKO), but giving up the guaranteed Gyarados KO for an 80% accuracy prediction is less likely.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1 (Focus Blast KO'd Archaludon via Sturdy+LO recoil, Dark Pulse KO'd Gengar). Klefki+Gyarados+Rotom-Heat vs Tinkaton+Blaziken+Rotom-W(Scarf). Rotom-W Scarf Volt Switch 4x guaranteed OHKOs Gyarados — must Protect or switch to Rotom-Heat. Rotom-Heat resists Volt Switch (0.5x). Blaziken Focus Sash already broken. Blaziken at +3 Speed para'd (137-181 effective). Gyarados 146 needs DD to outspeed Scarf Rotom-W (174-226). Rotom-Heat SpA at -4 — use status moves only, damage output negligible. Plan: burn Blaziken to neuter it (burn+Intimidate=0.25x Atk), then DD Gyarados and sweep. Preserve Rotom-Heat for Rotom-W matchup. Tinkaton at 38% para on bench — finish with Dazzling Gleam or Waterfall if it comes in.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Rotom-Heat at SpA -4 is non-threatening offensively but still alive. Focus fire with Hydro Pump (2x, Light Screen halves to ~1x) and Close Combat (physical, ignores Light Screen) to KO it. Blaziken paralyzed (50% fail) but if it moves, Close Combat finishes Rotom-Heat. Gyarados is bigger threat but 0.5x to both our moves; better to eliminate Rotom-Heat first and handle Gyarados with Rotom-Wash's 4x Volt Switch next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent brought Klefki (Prankster, Light Clay, screens) + Rotom-Heat (Expert Belt, Timid, SpA -4 after 2 Overheats). Back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, Intimidate). My back: Rotom-Wash (Choice Scarf, Timid). Screens: Light Screen 2 turns, Reflect 5 turns. Blaziken: Focus Sash intact, Speed +3, Atk -1, paralyzed. Rotom-Heat SpA -4 makes it non-threat; Gyarados main danger with Waterfall 2x Blaziken. Plan: KO Rotom-Heat with focused physical+special attack, then Rotom-Wash Volt Switch (4x) Gyarados. Tinkaton paralyzed, Atk -1, low utility. Archaludon fainted.

decisions.rationale: Klefki is dead this turn to Flare Blitz regardless. Use Prankster TWave on Rotom-W to permanently remove the 4x Volt Switch speed threat. Gyarados DDs freely — both foes' STABs are 0.5x vs Water/Flying with -1 Atk. After DD, Gyarados at 219 Spe outspeeds all and Waterfall KOs Blaziken next turn, then sweeps para'd Tinkaton + Rotom-W.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gengar-Mega fainted T1. Rotom-Heat fainted T7. Remaining: Klefki(23%, screens expiring) + Gyarados(84%, LO). Opponent: Blaziken(68%, para, +4 Spe, -1 Atk/Def/SpD, Focus Sash broken, can't dmg Gyarados 0.5x STABs), Rotom-W(81%, Scarf, Hydro Pump locked), Tinkaton(38%, para, bench). Gyarados at +1 Spe (219) outspeeds Blaziken(165-217) and para'd Rotom-W(87-113). Win con: DD now, sweep from T9. Blaziken Protect → +5 Spe(192-253) could outspeed but still can't KO Gyarados. If Rotom-W switches out this turn, TWave misses but Gyarados +1 still likely outspeeds Scarf Rotom-W (219 vs 174-226, only loses if raw 147+).

decisions.rationale: Focus fire on Klefki (23% HP) to secure the KO and create a favorable 2v1 vs Gyarados. Rotom-Wash is Choice-locked into Hydro Pump; targeting Klefki for neutral is better than 0.5x into Gyarados. Blaziken Flare Blitz is 2x SE vs Klefki. Even with Reflect halving physical damage, combined damage should KO Klefki. Blaziken's Focus Sash survives Gyarados Waterfall. Next turn Rotom-Wash Volt Switch (4x) pressures Gyarados heavily to close out the game.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Opponent brought Klefki (Prankster, Light Clay, screens) + Rotom-Heat (Expert Belt, Timid, SpA -4 after 2 Overheats). Back: Gyarados (Life Orb, Jolly, Intimidate). My back: Rotom-Wash (Choice Scarf, Timid). Rotom-Wash is Choice-locked into Hydro Pump. Blaziken: Focus Sash intact, Speed +4, Atk -1, Def -1, SpD -1, paralyzed. Screens: Light Screen 1 turn, Reflect 4 turns. Plan: KO Klefki with focused fire, then Rotom-Wash Volt Switch (4x) Gyarados to close. Gyarados main danger is Waterfall 2x Blaziken, but Focus Sash absorbs one hit. Klefki at 23% HP is priority target. Rotom-Heat fainted, non-threat after SpA -4.

decisions.rationale: Waterfall KOs Blaziken at 62% even through burn (+1 Atk ×1.5, burn ×0.5, net 63-147% > 62%). If Blaziken Protects, I take the same Hydro Pump+burn chip as any play. If it doesn't, I remove the threat immediately and face only locked NVE Hydro Pump 1v1. DD risks taking 43% chip if Blaziken attacks, potentially dying before I can KO. No 3-turn line survives the chip math.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Only Gyarados remains (61% brn, +1/+1, LO). Opponent: Blaziken(62%, para, +5 Spe→+6 after this turn, -1 Atk/Def/SpD, Sash broken, NVE vs Gyarados), Rotom-W(81%, Scarf, Hydro Pump locked, 0.5x vs Gyarados). Hydro Pump does 17-32% to Gyarados. Win con: KO Blaziken ASAP, then 1v1 Rotom-W (locked NVE). Gyarados +2 Spe (292) outspeeds Blaziken +6 para (max 290). Burn halves physical damage — Waterfall +1/burn does 63-147% to Blaziken, KO at 62%. Chip budget: ~2 turns max of Hydro Pump+burn before death.

decisions.rationale: Blaziken at 62% HP cannot survive Gyarados Waterfall (Focus Sash inactive). Attacking both risks Blaziken KO if Gyarados survives (28-62% damage vs 61% HP). Protect preserves Blaziken, Rotom-Wash chips Gyarados. Next turn switch Rotom-Wash to Tinkaton to break Choice lock, then Volt Switch 4x Gyarados to close.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gyarados last mon, burned, Life Orb, +1/+1 after Dragon Dance. Rotom-Wash Choice-locked Hydro Pump, must switch to unlock Volt Switch (4x Gyarados). Blaziken Focus Sash useless at 62% HP. Plan: Protect Blaziken turn 9, switch Rotom-Wash to Tinkaton turn 10 to break lock, switch back Rotom-Wash turn 11 for Volt Switch KO. Gyarados burn + Life Orb recoil = ~18% residual per turn.

decisions.rationale: Waterfall guaranteed KOs Blaziken (69.75% min > 62% even through burn + -1 Def). But using it now means Gyarados dies to Hydro Pump+LO+burn (~35-44% > 30% HP, 80% Hydro hits). Protect blocks Hydro Pump, only burn ticks (~6%), Gyarados survives at ~24%. Next turn Blaziken's Protect is further reduced; Waterfall KOs it. Win path needs Hydro Pump miss (20%) at some point — Protect buys an extra survival turn to reach that while keeping Gyarados alive and weakening Blaziken's Protect.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 endgame: Gyarados alone vs Blaziken+Rotom-W. Waterfall+1/burn/-1Def KOs Blaziken guaranteed (69.75% min > 62%). Hydro Pump does 19-28% to Gyarados (0.5x). Gyarados dies to Hydro+LO+burn if it attacks and Hydro connects. Win requires Hydro Pump miss (20% fail) at some point. Blaziken para 25% full para chance. Blaziken Protect already reduced from turn 9 use. Rotom-W Scarf-locked Hydro Pump, cannot switch moves. Opponent has Tinkaton (38% par) on bench — could switch in to avoid wasting Hydro Pump on Protect. Gyarados +1 Spe (219) is slower than Blaziken +6 para (220-290) and speed-ties Rotom-W Scarf (174-226).

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash is Choice-locked into NVE Hydro Pump; switching to Tinkaton breaks the lock for next turn's Volt Switch KO. Blaziken's attacks are NVE and halved by Reflect, so it must Protect to survive Gyarados's Waterfall, even with reduced success rate.
decisions.notebook: Game 2: Gyarados last mon, burned, Life Orb, +1/+1 after Dragon Dance. Rotom-Wash Choice-locked into Hydro Pump, must switch to unlock Volt Switch (4x Gyarados). Blaziken Focus Sash useless at 62% HP. Plan: Protect Blaziken turn 10, switch Rotom-Wash to Tinkaton to break lock. Turn 11: switch Tinkaton back to Rotom-Wash for Volt Switch KO, or Blaziken attacks if Gyarados is low enough. Gyarados burn + Life Orb recoil = ~18% residual per turn.

decisions.rationale: Waterfall into Blaziken is the only line that can remove the +6 Spe threat. With burn (0.5x) and Blaziken -1 Def (1.5x), net 0.75x on 71.7-136.8% range = 54-103%, giving ~75% KO chance vs 62% HP. Gyarados dies to burn+LO regardless, but KOing Blaziken is the most proactive play and best chance if opponent misplays endgame.

reflections.summary: Lost because Gengar-Mega and Rotom-Heat fell early, leaving Gyarados as the sole remaining wincon. Gyarados got burned by Blaziken's Flare Blitz on turn 8, and with burn + Life Orb recoil it was doomed even after a Dragon Dance. Klefki's Thunder Wave was wasted on Rotom-W (Electric immunity), and a crit Hydro Pump removed Klefki immediately. By the time Gyarados traded with Blaziken on turn 11, Rotom-Wash survived at 81% with no answer left.
reflections.adjustment: For game 3, do not let Gyarados absorb Flare Blitz—lead Klefki for Reflect to blunt Blaziken's damage and use Thunder Wave on Blaziken/Tinkaton, not Rotom-W. Preserve Gengar-Mega longer; Shadow Tag should trap Blaziken early to prevent Speed Boost Protect cycling. Consider whether Gengar-Mega is the right Mega here at all—its frailty and lack of relevant resistances against Blaziken/Rotom-W make it a liability; if an alternative Mega exists, evaluate it. Prioritize KOing Rotom-W before it can sp

For game 3: consider leading Klefki + Gengar-Mega to TWave Blaziken and trap it; Rotom-Heat is strong into Tinkaton/Archaludon but must avoid Scarf Hydro Pump from Rotom-W.

reflections.summary: The game was won as Blaziken's Speed Boost and Rotom-Wash's offensive pressure systematically eliminated the opponent's core, culminating in a turn 11 mutual KO between Blaziken and Gyarados that left the opponent with no remaining Pokemon while I retained Tinkaton and Rotom-Wash.
